title: Bodycam Shows Chicago Officer Shot by Her Own Partner
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
Chicago, Illinois — On June 5, 2025, Chicago Police Officers Krystal Rivera and her partner, Carlos Baker, were on patrol on the city’s South Side. According to official accounts, they initiated what’s known as an investigatory stop after spotting a man they believed might be armed. When the man noticed the officers, he fled on foot, prompting Officer Rivera to immediately give chase, with Officer Baker close behind. The pursuit led them into an apartment building, where the suspect ran upstairs and into a unit, with both officers following within seconds. As they moved through the building, the situation escalated quickly. The suspect forced his way into an apartment, and the officers reached the door moments later. Officer Baker moved ahead and kicked the door open while Officer Rivera was just behind him in the hallway. Inside, there were indications of at least one other person, and at least one individual appeared to be holding a firearm. In that split-second, high-pressure moment, Officer Baker turned and fired a single shot. That round did not hit the suspect, it struck Officer Rivera, who was positioned behind him and had not yet entered the apartment.

Officer Baker radioed that shots had been fired and retreated briefly up the stairwell, calling for backup and medical assistance, at times stating he could not reach his partner, while remaining positioned on an upper stairwell. Roughly two minutes passed before he returned to Officer Rivera, who was lying wounded on the floor. The footage shows him eventually dragging her toward the building’s exit as other officers arrived. Notably, the released material does not clearly show any immediate medical aid being administered before additional units reached the scene. The case has sparked ongoing legal and public debate, fueled in part by a wrongful death lawsuit filed by Rivera’s family. The suit alleges a troubled personal history between the two officers and claims Baker failed to act to save her life, accusations his legal team strongly denies. Attorneys for the family have also questioned the completeness of the video release, arguing that key footage may still be missing. As the investigation continues, officials maintain the incident remains under active review, while the newly surfaced footage adds further complexity to an already deeply contested narrative.
